zh.title: Eve Air完成eVTOL首次部分過渡飛行並啟動推進系統
zh.summary: 巴西航空工業旗下的 Eve Air Mobility 於 2026 年 8 月 3 日完成其電動垂直起降原型機的首次部分過渡飛行。飛行過程中成功啟動推進推進系統，原型機持續飛行 3 分 9 秒，飛行距離約 0.84 海浬，高度達 90 英尺，速度穩定於 27 節。
body: 巴西航空工業（Embraer）旗下的 Eve Air Mobility 於 2026 年 8 月 3 日宣佈，其電動垂直起降（eVTOL）工程原型機在首次部分過渡飛行中，成功啟動了推進推進系統。根據該公司發布的資訊，該原型機在推進推進系統的支援下持續飛行了 3 分 9 秒。這次試飛啟動了飛機的後置推進螺旋槳，標誌著該原型機從垂直起降邁向依靠機翼升力前進飛行的過渡階段測試。
在本次飛行測試過程中，該 eVTOL 原型機在推進器轉速最高達 1,200 RPM 的情況下，飛行速度穩定在 27 節，地面最高速度達到 30 節。試飛期間，該飛行器共飛行了約 0.84 海浬，離地高度達到 90 英尺。該公司表示，本次試飛順利完成，驗證了 Eve 飛機設計的關鍵特性，並達成了初始過渡階段的重要技術指標。
Eve Air Mobility 執行長 Johann Bordais 表示，在飛行中成功啟動推進推進系統是開發歷程中的重要里程碑，驗證了飛機設計的核心部分。工程主管 Marcelo Basile 則補充指出，本次試飛蒐集到的各項資料，將為後續邁向更高速度及更複雜的過渡飛行測試提供支援，有助於持續擴大飛機的飛行包線。
目前 Eve 的飛行測試工程團隊正持續進行載荷與結構分析，以支援未來更廣泛的飛行測試。在接下來的幾週內，該公司預計將逐步擴大飛機的空速範圍，並執行更多包含推進器啟動的試飛作業。在完成飛機的飛行測試計畫後，該公司還計劃進行資料鏈測試，以驗證無線電鏈路效能，並支援速度最高達 50 節的飛行營運需求。

en.title: Eve Air Mobility Activates Pusher System in First eVTOL Partial Transition Flight
en.summary: Eve Air Mobility, a subsidiary of Embraer, announced on August 3, 2026, that its electric vertical takeoff and landing engineering prototype completed its first partial transition flight. During the three-minute and nine-second flight, the company successfully activated the aircraft's rear pusher propulsion system. The prototype covered approximately 0.84 nautical miles, reached an altitude of 90 feet above ground level, and stabilized at an airspeed of 27 knots while reaching a maximum ground speed of 30 knots.
body: Eve Air Mobility, a subsidiary of Embraer, announced on August 3, 2026, that its electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) engineering prototype completed its first partial transition flight while activating its pusher propulsion system. According to the company, the prototype flew for three minutes and nine seconds supported by the pusher propulsion system, marking the start of the transition phase from vertical takeoff to wing-borne flight.

During the flight test, the eVTOL prototype stabilized at an airspeed of 27 knots and achieved a maximum ground speed of 30 knots with the rear pusher propeller operating at up to 1,200 RPM. The aircraft covered approximately 0.84 nautical miles and climbed to an altitude of 90 feet above ground level. The company highlighted that the test successfully validated key performance targets for the initial transition phase.

Eve Air Mobility Chief Executive Officer Johann Bordais stated that activating the pusher propulsion system in flight validates a key aspect of the aircraft design. Head of Engineering Marcelo Basile noted that data collected during the test flight will support continued flight envelope expansion as the program advances toward higher airspeeds and more complex transition testing scenarios.

The flight test engineering team is continuing ongoing structural and loads analyses to support future envelope expansion. Over the coming weeks, Eve Air Mobility expects to expand the aircraft's airspeed envelope through additional test flights with pusher activation. Following this phase, the company plans to conduct datalink testing to evaluate radio link performance and support flight operations at speeds up to 50 knots.

zh.title: 西捷航空與客艙組員工會達成初步協議結束罷工
zh.summary: 西捷航空與代表客艙組員的加拿大公共員工工會8125分會於2026年8月3日達成初步協議，正式結束自8月2日展開的罷工行動。該起罷工曾造成航班取消與網路營運中斷。雙方達成協議後，該份初步協議將提交給工會成員進行批准投票，西捷航空亦展開航班恢復作業。
body: 加拿大西捷航空（WestJet）與代表客艙組員的加拿大公共員工工會（CUPE）8125分會於2026年8月3日達成初步協議。航空公司表示，該項協議順利讓近期引發的停工行動與全系統營運中斷告一段落，並結束了導致數百個航班取消的勞資僵局。
西捷航空的客艙組員先前於2026年8月2日正式發動罷工，工會當時強調未獲薪酬的工作內容是勞方爭取權益的核心重點之一。航空公司指出，在罷工與相關衝突期間，共造成約25萬名預計於8月長週末出行的旅客行程受到取消與干擾。
針對新達成的初步協議，加拿大公共員工工會8125分會主席 Alia Hussain 表示，這份協議代表了實質性的進展。工會說明，該協議改進了原有的航班點數制度，透過引進執勤時間津貼，更加認可客艙組員必須執行的各項工作，並提高相應的整體薪酬待遇。
該份初步協議在雙方達成一致後，將隨即提交給西捷航空客艙組員工會的全體成員進行批准投票。工會指出，舉辦批准投票的具體日期將於近期對外公布，投票結果將決定該項勞資協議是否正式生效。
西捷航空執行長 Alexis von Hoensbroech 表示，對於能夠找到前進的協議感到高興，並稱該協議反映了員工的辛勤工作與專業精神。他同時對營運中斷給旅客與員工帶來的困擾致歉，並強調公司的營運團隊正在全力以赴恢復正常服務，協助旅客儘快前往目的地。

en.title: WestJet Ends Cabin Crew Strike Following Tentative Agreement with Union
en.summary: WestJet and CUPE 8125, the union representing cabin crew staff, reached a tentative agreement on August 3, 2026, bringing an end to the strike action that began on August 2. The strike action had led to flight cancellations and network-wide operational disruptions across the airline's system. The newly reached tentative deal will now be submitted to WestJet cabin crew union members for a ratification vote, while airline management works to restore regular flight operations.
body: Canadian carrier WestJet and CUPE 8125, the labor union representing the airline's cabin crew staff, reached a tentative collective agreement on August 3, 2026, effectively bringing an end to the active work stoppage. The airline stated that the new agreement closes the network-wide operational disruptions that had resulted in hundreds of flight cancellations across its schedule.

WestJet cabin crew members had officially initiated strike action on August 2, 2026, pointing to unpaid work during required duties as a major priority in their labor dispute. In statements issued during the disruption, WestJet noted that the work stoppage had affected an estimated 250,000 guests whose August long weekend travel plans were cancelled or impacted.

Commenting on the newly reached deal, CUPE 8125 President Alia Hussain said the tentative agreement represents meaningful progress for the workforce. The union explained that the agreement improves upon the existing flight credit system by introducing a dedicated duty period premium, better recognizing the various duties required of cabin crew members and providing general compensation increases.

With the tentative terms agreed upon by both negotiating teams, the agreement will now be presented to WestJet cabin crew union members for a formal ratification vote. The union confirmed that the precise date for holding the ratification vote will be announced to members shortly.

WestJet Chief Executive Officer Alexis von Hoensbroech said he was pleased that an agreement to move forward had been established, adding that the outcome reflects the hard work and professionalism of employees. He offered an apology to impacted passengers for the frustration caused by the flight disruptions and affirmed that airline operational teams are working hard to restore standard flight operations as quickly as possible.
